An angle that measures less than 90°.

A tool for measuring angles in degrees.

cards.front: How many degrees are in a full turn? A straight angle? A right angle?

cards.back: An angle that turns through 1/360 of a circle.

cards.front: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
How many lines of symmetry does a square have? A rectangle that is not a square?
cards.back: A square has 4. The rectangle has 2.

cards.front: How do you use a protractor?
cards.back: Put the center on the vertex. Line up one ray with 0°. Read the scale where the other ray crosses.

cards.front: An angle is split into two smaller angles. How are the measures related?
cards.back: The two smaller measures add up to the measure of the whole angle.

cards.front: What makes a triangle a right triangle?
cards.back: It has one right angle.

cards.front: Which has parallel sides: a rectangle or a triangle?
cards.back: A rectangle has 2 pairs of parallel sides. A triangle has none.
95°. It is greater than 90°.

cards.front: Does a longer ray make a bigger angle?
cards.back: No. The size of an angle depends on how far one ray turns from the other, not on the length of the rays.

cards.front: Is the diagonal of a rectangle (not a square) a line of symmetry?
cards.back: No. The two parts do not match when you fold on the diagonal.

cards.front: An angle measures 50°. Did you read 130° on the protractor?
cards.back: Check which scale starts at 0° on your first ray. An acute angle must be less than 90°.
